name: coordination-protocol-contract-package
description: The CPCP contract home: envelopes, refusal taxonomy, idempotency, method conventions, layer authority, operation identity and scopes, plus the base OWL ontology.
note: The contract home carries spec/ and ontology/ instead of a demo of its own. It answers no RPC and serves no seam, but it does serve the scope vocabulary that every downstream .cpcp manifest cites -- so it carries a 'services' manifest whose seams list is empty and whose scope_definitions are the definition of record. The layout every CPCP package repo follows is specified in spec/repo-format.md, and the four roles a unit is made of in spec/roles.md.

standing_on.note: Base owns the shapes; CPCP is the transport of the grant and the packaging of it. Do not restate the base here.

scopes.rule: A scope answers two questions at once: which way the call runs, and how far. Calls beyond the pod: dependency. Calls within it: pod_internal_dependencies. Serves beyond the pod: services. Serves within it: pod_internal_services. Direction decides the field -- a calling scope carries depends_on, a serving scope carries seams. The method contract is identical at every scope; reach is not.
scopes.change_rule: Adding a scope to a seam is a contract change: update the seam's gate and whatever runs its conformance matrix, never just the compose file.

worked_example.note: Illustration, not specification. CPCP is not this deployment; another one's map would name entirely different seams and be equally correct. Kept because a shape is easier to read from one filled-in example than from prose. See spec/scopes.md note [1].

unmapped.because: Live in magentic-stack (switchyard.route, cpcp.ready, cid) but absent from the map above. Browser-local credential routing, not pod-network traffic, so none of the three scopes is obviously correct. Needs a contract decision.
